purpose: derive the bank service operations from the integration material

notes: The IVR integration document (section 6) was not in the material I was given. Only BRIEF.md, the flow drawing and the first part of test-customers.json were. So I used the fallback for every service: method POST, with the path made from the service name by turning dots into slashes (cards.list -> /cards/list, cards.balance -> /cards/balance, statement.week.get -> /statement/week/get, statement.week.decide -> /statement/week/decide, statement.week.change -> /statement/week/change, contact.email.get -> /contact/email/get, statement.pdf.send -> /statement/pdf/send). If the integration document is available, its paths, methods and request fields take precedence over these.

The material does not name the request body fields directly. I took them from the test data: customerNo is the customer key, cardNumber is the masked card number from cards.list that keys the card-level services, and newStatementWeek is the second key of statement.week.decide and statement.week.change. statement.pdf.send and contact.email.get are keyed by customer only in the test data, so their body holds only customerNo.

The masking differs between services. cards.list and statement.week.get return "540000******1234", while cards.balance returns "5400********1234". Always call with the cardNumber exactly as cards.list returns it, because that is the key the test data uses.
statementWeek and statementDay are integers in statement.week.get and statement.week.decide, but strings in statement.week.change. I left both exactly as the test data has them.

Response bodies are the test data's own. In the part of the test data I could see, only HTTP 200 success answers appear. Other customers in the full test-customers.json may have different statuses, error bodies, exitState values or a 'gecikmeSaniye' delay. The mock must return those exactly per customer and card, but I could not see them, so I did not invent any.
No authentication or fixed headers appear in the material, so auth_headers is empty.
The test-data description says it follows 'the 2026-10-01 service contract'. I treated that contract as the newest valid version.
